1.why: Reset tokens are bound to the recovering session via session.resetHash and verified with safeEqual(digest(token), session.resetHash) before password change.

2.why: Each session stores its own resetHash; another user's session has a different hash so the same reset code cannot authorize their flow.

3.why: Password reset only mutates INTERNAL_ACCOUNT.passwordHash and the current session stage; other entries in the sessions Map are never invalidated.

4.why: Bun.serve is started with TLS cert/key and HSTS is set, but no explicit minimum TLS version is configured in code.

5.why: Passwords use argon2id and reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 digests; protection is hashing rather than encryption, but algorithms are appropriate.

6.why: Simulated recovery messages are generic and only carry the one-time secrets, with no extra account PII embedded in the email content.

7.why: Server validates email/token/password shapes; client inserts all dynamic values with createTextNode/textContent and never innerHTML.

8.why: Navigation stays on same origin (location.origin links and history.replaceState to '/'); no user-controlled redirect targets exist.

9.why: There are no HTML email templates; delivery is simulated as plain text logs without interpolating user input as markup.

10.why: Authorization secrets, reset tokens, and MFA codes are returned in API JSON and deliberately printed in the client Logs panel.

11.why: Runtime password hashes use argon2id, but MFA_CODE is hardcoded plaintext and the demo passwordHash lives in source.

12.why: A fixed test account is embedded and MFA is always the static code 246810, so default/second-factor credentials are effectively allowed.

13.why: Channel, reset-verify, login, and MFA paths each increment failure counters and lock after MAX_RECOVERY_ATTEMPTS (5) for LOCK_TTL.

14.why: recovery/start always returns the same ok/message regardless of whether the email matches INTERNAL_ACCOUNT, with a constant delay.

15.why: Reset tokens come from randomBytes(32).toString('base64url') and are bound to the issuing session via its resetHash.
